comments.author: 99catgames
comments.body:
This is great, and I appreciate that there's a free license collection. Though it says "over 300" in that collection and I'm only seeing 191 right now. 

For the paid licenses, is that $3.99 or whatever forever but only for that collection? The free collection is a mix-n-match, which is nice, but also, who needs 100 potions? Or 111 weapons? I need like 10 weapons and 4 potions and just 1 chair, etc. Why not have an option for a mix-n-match collection where you get a certain number of items from any collection?

Also, just FYI when I go to click purchase (just testing, not actually purchasing), I get a server error.

replies.author: W0RKABLE
replies.body:
Thanks a lot for the feedback!  
You're right in the number discrepancy, I pulled some free items back into refinement, will be fixed soon.  
  
Yes when you buy a collection it is forever, and you also get a more permissive license.  
  
The composition of collections is something I'm taking feedback for, to figure out what people actually need. I could imagine games where you need 100 potions, even though probably not many :D There are more generic collections as well, such as the survival one. This aims to support games that would be about survival and has a mix of related items.  
  
Mix-n-match is a good idea, I will definitely consider that.

Error will be fixed, thanks for testing it!

Really appreciate the feedback, again. If you send me a DM I'll give you any collection of your choosing for free :)

comments.author: No_Surround_4662
comments.body:
Looks good really good, can see it being used a lot. Should probably allow users to select multiple sprites and edit them at the same time - same as the pixel palette at the bottom of the screen. What LLM did you use to create the sprites? Is it retrodiffusion or is it a pixel lora with flux?

Bugs:

Open it in the modal, close it - try and open the same in the same modal - it doesn't open again (probably flag isn't set to 0)

The 'preview' panel for the sprite, you want to disable CSS select on the image - it messes up the drag functionality and you can get stuck in the drag scene

Personal preference, you've scaled out about 0.95 or 0.9 for the list preview as 'default'. I don't think this is good because the anti-aliasing fucks up the image. Keep the scale at 1 for the default preview - otherwise all the sprites look a bit shite until you hover them.

replies.author: W0RKABLE
replies.body:
Wow super in depth, thanks!  
Thanks for spotting these bugs, will fix them ASAP, I actually haven't seen the anti-aliasing at work, might be because I'm working on a higher res screen.

The process is actually a bit more custom, I didn't like results from retrodiff, or flux lora. Especially when it comes to smaller sizes, like 32x32 on Pixelrepo. The current base images are combination of both midjourney and gpt-image, but they go though a lot of processing afterwards.
